title: Duke–Schulze-Pillot: the upper bound of Lemma 5(ii) and a conditional Theorem 3(ii)
abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization around W. Duke and R. Schulze-Pillot, Representation of integers by positive ternary quadratic forms and equidistribution of lattice points on ellipsoids (Invent. Math. 99, 1990). q(x) = ½ xᵗAx for a symmetric integer 3 × 3 matrix A with q > 0 on ℚ³ \ {0}, h ∈ ℚ³, r(q, h, n) = #{x ∈ h + ℤ³ : q(x) = n} and, for F ⊆ ℝ³, r(q, F, h, n) = #{x ∈ h + ℤ³ : q(x) = n, x/√n ∈ F}. Unconditional results: card_divisors_le_rpow (d(n) ≤ C_ε n^ε); repCount_le (r(q, h, n) ≤ C_ε n^{1/2+ε} for n ≥ 1); average_le (the same bound for every nonnegatively weighted average of such counts, which includes r(spn_N q, h, n): this is the upper half of Lemma 5(ii)). Conditional results: thm3_ii (Theorem 3(ii), r(q, F, h, n) = R(n) μ(F) + O(n^{1/2 − 1/175 + ε}) for n ≥ 1 in a set S) and spn_upper (R(n) ≤ C_ε n^{1/2+ε}) are proved under two hypotheses that are NOT proved here: hThm1, the estimate of Theorem 1 of the paper (|r(q, F, h, n) − r(q, h, n) μ(F)| ≤ C (n^{−1/175} r(q, h, n) + n^{1/2−1/175+ε}) on S), and hThm3i, the estimate of Theorem 3(i) (|r(q, h, n) − R(n)| ≤ C n^{1/2−1/28+ε} on S); R stands for r(spn_N q, h, n), μF ∈ [0, 1] for μ(F), and S for the restricted set of n. The lower bound n^{1/2−ε} ≪ r(spn_N q, h, n) of Lemma 5(ii) (Siegel's ineffective bound) is not formalized.
